      "utf8_content": "# CM24: a source-only rational-gauge selector fails by one trace residue

Status: paper derivation, not independently reviewed. This tests only the
previously frozen full-system rational-gauge rule. It does not select or
refute the period coefficient kappa and does not evaluate Y or Z.

Canonical owner: EM-DIRECT-18F24A. Support author:
EM-CM24CONN-63E74C9D, using the existing RA. Root selected the source-only
contiguous/Green direction and the requirement that a selector precede any
attempt to solve the endpoint candidate. The finite gauge class and the
derivation below are this support author's contribution. No global novelty
claim is made; the trace-residue obstruction is standard algebra.

## 1. Exact frozen question and inputs

The preceding file
CM24_SOURCE_GAUSS_RATIONAL_GAUGE_SELECTOR_PREFLIGHT_FREEZE.json fixes:

    X_ij(z)=u_ij+v_ij z+w_ij/z+t_ij/(1-z),
    X_12(1/2)=1, gamma != 0,

with 16 rational matrix coefficients and one scalar gamma. Its full
identity is

    X'+X A0-A0 X = gamma B0.                           (1)

Every coefficient row after multiplication by z^2(1-z)^2, through
degree 5, is required. This is a finite affine algebraic rule, not a
family of numerical period fits. No matrix solve is needed below.

Here z is the external Gauss argument. Write p=6m+1 in the original
prime family and retain a=-m, b=-2m, c=-3m as literal integers before
reduction. The plus parameters are exactly (a,b+p,c+p). The already
proved normalized terminating polynomials are

    h_minus(z)=binom(3m,m)
       sum_(k=0)^m (-m)_k(-2m)_k/[(-3m)_k k!] z^k,

    h_plus(z)=(-1)^m binom(4m,m)
       sum_(k=0)^m (-m)_k(4m+1)_k/[(3m+1)_k k!] z^k.

The actual x-polynomials are h_minus(rho(x)), h_plus(rho(x)), with
rho=x(4x-3)^2. All denominators through k=m are p-units; both
polynomials equal 1 at z=1 exactly and reduce to the prescribed
normalized source h(z). Those are already proved inputs from Source
0c62e03e04ed73916527bb31a231a69fa00e5fe0, not newly recomputed claims.

Delta=(h_plus-h_minus)/p is formed coefficientwise in Z_(p) BEFORE
modulo p. It has the fixed normalization Delta(1)=0 and the fixed
binomial-origin value delta_g. Neither Y nor a T half-boundary occurs
in this construction.

## 2. The exact inhomogeneous source equation

For ordinary rational z, put

    L(a,b;c)=z(1-z)D_z^2
             +[c-(a+b+1)z]D_z-ab.

Directly subtracting its coefficients, without evaluating a period,
gives the exact identity

    L(a,b+p;c+p)-L(a,b;c)
         =p R_m,    R_m=(1-z)D_z+m.                   (2)

Both source polynomials satisfy their respective terminating Gauss
equations. The normalization constants do not alter those equations.
Consequently, over Z_(p)[z],

    L_minus [(h_plus-h_minus)/p] = -R_m h_plus.        (3)

This keeps the complete terminating polynomials, their top terms and
their origin normalizations. There is no division by p in F_p.
Reduction uses m=-1/6 as a FIELD SCALAR only in operator coefficients;
the terminating integer degree m is not replaced by a fractional power.

Define

    L0=z(1-z)D_z^2+(1/2-3z/2)D_z-1/18,
    R0=(1-z)D_z-1/6.

Then the actual source lift satisfies the exact reduced equation

    L0 Delta = -R0 h.                                (4)

This is new explicit source-side information for the proposed selector.
It does not assert an equation for T, change the actual forcing, or
produce a value for the remaining Omega moment.

For completeness, use the companion vector v=(h,D_z h)^t and matrix

    A(a,b,c;z) =
       [ 0,                        1                         ]
       [ ab/[z(1-z)], ((a+b+1)z-c)/[z(1-z)]                 ].

Its exact parameter difference is

    A_plus-A_minus = p B_m,
    B_m = [0,0; -m/[z(1-z)], -1/z].

If delta_v=(v_plus-v_minus)/p, ordinary differentiation gives

    delta_v' = A_minus delta_v+B_m v_plus.

After reduction, therefore,

    delta_v' = A0 delta_v+B0 v,
    A0 = [0,1; 1/[18z(1-z)], (3z-1)/[2z(1-z)]],
    B0 = [0,0; 1/[6z(1-z)], -1/z].                   (5)

Equation (5) is exactly equivalent to (4), including the sign. In
particular the candidate gauge is a full two-dimensional-system rule,
not merely an identity assumed for the one prescribed solution v.

## 3. One necessary coefficient kills the frozen rule

Take the matrix trace of (1). Over every commutative coefficient field,
tr(X A0-A0 X)=0. Equation (5) gives tr B0=-1/z. Thus (1) requires

    (tr X)' = -gamma/z.                              (6)

For ANY rational function f(z), the coefficient of z^(-1) in its
Laurent expansion of f'(z) at z=0 is zero: that coefficient could only
come from differentiating its z^0 term, whose derivative is zero.
This argument works in characteristic zero and in positive
characteristic. It does not rely on numerical integration, analytic
branches, or a bound on the rational function's poles.

Taking the coefficient of z^(-1) in (6) therefore forces

    gamma=0.                                         (7)

This contradicts the frozen gamma != 0 condition. It kills the full
finite class before a linear solve, and in fact proves the stronger
statement that NO rational matrix X can satisfy (1) with nonzero
gamma. The affine normalization X_12(1/2)=1 cannot repair this trace
defect. No claim about existence or uniqueness at gamma=0 is needed
or made.

The same residue argument applies separately over every original
F_p: 2 and 3 are units, the matrices in (5) are well defined as rational
functions, and -gamma/z has residue -gamma. This is not transport of a
Q rank computation to F_p and is not a campaign of prime examples.

Over a characteristic-zero logarithmic extension a necessary trace
would be -gamma log(z)+constant. Such an extension is OUTSIDE the
frozen rational rule and has not been constructed here.

## 4. What this does and does not settle

The tested source-only normalization rule has an exact algebraic
obstruction: the simultaneous b,c deformation changes the trace
connection at z=0 by a nonzero logarithmic residue. It cannot be
removed by a rational infinitesimal gauge on the full rank-two source
system. Adding origin or endpoint constants to that full-system
gauge does not change the residue argument.

There is no contradiction with the existence of the actual
polynomial Delta in (4). A particular inhomogeneous solution for the
prescribed normalized h is weaker than a rational matrix gauge that
acts on EVERY solution of the two-dimensional homogeneous system.
The terminating source and its fixed origin/endpoint conditions are
retained. This proof does not discard their actual solution.

In particular gamma has NOT been identified with the target period
kappa in

    3Y=kappa Pi,  Pi=ell(U).

Even a successful source gauge would still require a separately proved
relative Green bridge before making that identification. Failure of
this gauge cannot rule out kappa=0, a nonzero universal kappa, or some
other source-dependent endpoint relation. It is not the old
homogeneous-adjoint no-go or another T four-column calculation.

The next missing input is now more precise: a finite SOURCE-SPECIFIC
relative/contiguous certificate, valid on the prescribed normalized
terminating solution rather than on the whole rank-two solution
space, together with a proved bridge from its normalization to the
fixed endpoint functional ell. An arbitrary full-system rational
gauge, even with larger rational poles, cannot supply that input.
No such narrower certificate is asserted or selected in this unit.

Thus the earlier one-period proposal remains NOT_EXECUTABLE. The
arbitrary-height rational-kappa/CRT issue has not been bypassed:
there are no field samples or fitted congruences here, and no
mathematical impossibility statement about that kappa.

## 5. Execution, scope and next action

The candidate rule was saved before this written derivation; structural
reasoning selected the rule before that freeze. No blind or authenticated
preregistration is claimed. This unit used paper coefficient subtraction,
companion-system algebra and one Laurent coefficient. No scientific code,
prime evaluation, checker, Hart run, matrix solve, new owner, Task, claim,
branch, remote Source or RA mutation occurred. File saving and hashing are
ordinary persistence operations.

All z, x, matrices and arithmetic lifts remain external typed observers
under P000/Heartbeat X6 and joint-relation preservation. No Native spatial
axis, physical-time, resource lowerbound, Native acceptance or completion
claim follows.

Return this finite-rule rejection and the narrower missing input to Root.
Do not enlarge the class or start another selector. Y, Z, C, tau, F_CM
and the original mathematical/user parent remain OPEN.

      "utf8_content": "# Present nonauthor Driver check: source Gauss deformation and trace obstruction

fitting; the author selected and froze the full-system gauge class and
derived the equations. I did not derive or author that proposed rule before
this review. My prior contributions to a different CM24 p13 witness and
control integration are disclosed; this is not blind independent discovery.

Disposition: PASS for the exact source-deformation identities and the
nonexistence of a rational full-system infinitesimal gauge with the frozen
nonzero scalar. This is not a period-kappa no-go or evaluation of Y/Z.

I read the complete 8706-byte paper
CM24_SOURCE_GAUSS_DEFORMATION_TRACE_OBSTRUCTION.md, its preflight freeze,
and its bounded handoff. The paper's SHA256 is
966f406c0e698ea56a1958c7a8c88c5928a707e06537b3ef5eeb5b5bb936c190.

0c62e03e04ed73916527bb31a231a69fa00e5fe0; no old checker or prime is rerun.

For p=6m+1, the minus parameters are (-m,-2m,-3m); the plus b,c are
b+p=4m+1,c+p=3m+1. In
L=z(1-z)D²+[c-(a+b+1)z]D-ab, shifting b,c by p changes the derivative
coefficient by p(1-z) and the constant by -ap=mp. Thus the exact operator
difference is p[(1-z)D+m]. From Lplus hplus=0 and Lminus hminus=0,
division coefficientwise over Z_(p) gives Lminus Delta=-[(1-z)D+m]hplus.
This division occurs before modp. The fixed normalization Delta(1)=0 is
retained; the operator equation alone does not select an arbitrary solution.

Reducing m=-1/6 in operator coefficients gives a=1/6,b=1/3,c=1/2,
so ab=1/18 and a+b+1=3/2. Consequently
L0=z(1-z)D²+(1/2-3z/2)D-1/18 and
L0 Delta=-[(1-z)D-1/6]h. This substitution concerns field coefficients,
not replacement of the terminating integer degree by a fractional exponent.

The companion matrix is [0,1; ab/(z(1-z)),((a+b+1)z-c)/(z(1-z))].
Its exact difference divided by p has lower row
[-m/(z(1-z)),-1/z], hence B0=[0,0;1/(6z(1-z)),-1/z].
The author's signs agree in the scalar and companion equations: the
inhomogeneous derivative equation is delta_v'=A0 delta_v+B0 v.

For the frozen identity X'+XA0-A0X=gamma B0, cyclicity of trace over a
commutative field removes the commutator and forces (trX)'=-gamma/z.
Expand a rational function at z=0 as a Laurent series with a finite
principal part. The coefficient of z^(-1) in its derivative can only arise
from differentiating its z^0 coefficient, so is zero. This argument works
in characteristic zero and in each original Fp with p!=2,3. It does not
transport a rank computation over Q to finite fields. The right side has
coefficient -gamma, forcing gamma=0. This contradicts the frozen nonzero
condition, independently of X12(1/2)=1, and applies even to arbitrary
rational X outside the original finite pole class. No matrix solve,
finite-field sample or numerical integration is required.

The conclusion quantifies over gauges acting on the entire rank-two
homogeneous system. It does not forbid the actual normalized particular
polynomial Delta; requiring a full-system gauge is stronger. Gamma was
never identified with the proposed endpoint-period kappa. No conclusion
that kappa=0, that all kappa fail, or that Y/Z is evaluated follows. Enlarging
rational pole bounds cannot fix this trace obstruction. A logarithmic
extension or a source-specific relative certificate is a different question;
neither has been constructed or selected here. Arbitrary-height kappa
cannot be inferred from a finite list of field examples.

The step therefore adds the exact inhomogeneous source equation and removes

ell functional, remains missing. The prior one-period candidate remains
